Title: Setting off
Text: During the four years of my PhD I spent a lot of time dreaming of vanlife, and watching a lot of youtube videos for inspiration. On the 13th of July 2019 I bought a Mercedes Sprinter (long wheel base) for £7,000. It had been used as a delivery van previously and had 160k miles on the clock but was in good condition. I converted it into a campervan by cladding the interior with pine, cutting holes in the sides for windows, and putting in beds, a kitchen, electric (solar powered) and storage spaces. I built a composting toilet and fitted some back seats for the children which I picked up from a guy who was taking them out of an old minivan, also for a camper conversion. In October that year we finally set off, planning to travel the whole of Europe — if only we'd known covid was coming!

Title: A España
Text: We drove down to the south coast in one go with a Dover-Calais ferry booked. We were giving a lift to a friend of ours who's parents lived near Düsseldorf so we passed quickly through France, Belgium and The Netherlands, stopping for a few ours at Doel (near Antwerp), an abandoned port town covered with street art. After Düsseldorf we headed through Luxembourg and down through France to Andorra.

Title: La costa al desierto
Text: My first view of Spain came with blue skies and sunshine as we headed down the Piranese into Catalunya. Just hours after being wrapped up warm for the cold and cloud of Andorra la Vella we were sitting in the sun at a café in Montserrat, and the next day lying on the beach in Badalona. In six weeks we experienced the cities of Valencia, Murcia, Alicante and Almeria, besides many smaller towns; we drank wine and beer, and ate churros, in local cafés; we experienced wild smimming in thermally heated rivers and pools; we saw forrests, mountains, beaches and deserts; we played cowboys in Texas Hollywood, Tabernas; and we had Christmas on a secluded beach near Nerja where we were able to lie in the sun and swim in the sea. What an introduction to the country!
